newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentina's Cavallo vows to fight court "maneuver".
newsitem.headline: Argentina's Cavallo vows to fight court "maneuver".

text.p: Former Argentine Economy Minister Domingo Cavallo vowed in comments published Tuesday to fight indictment over a postal tender, denouncing it as a "maneuver" by a cabinet minister and a postal tycoon.
Cavallo, sacked last July, told Clarin newspaper from the United States: "I'll return to Buenos Aires Wednesday to give more details about this maneuver against me."

Cavallo is campaigning for a seat in Congress in October elections on an anti-corruption platform whose main target is private postal tycoon Alfredo Yabran, whom he says is aided by Interior Minister Carlos Corach and other senior officials.

"I can tell you we are going to appeal. This case and others are evidence of the joint manipulation of the courts by Corach and Yabran," he told Clarin. "My hopes are diminishing that there can ever be justice for me in Argentina."
The irascible former minister, who has about 20 court cases pending, was indicted over a tender for postal services for state mortgage lender Banco Hipotecario in 1993.
Cavallo annulled it and gave the contract to state post office Encotesa at 40 cents a letter, rather than renew a contract held by Yabran's firm OCASA at $1.80 per letter.
He said it was "amazing" that he should be suspected of corruption when he saved the bank an estimated $18 million.

But Federal Judge Norberto Oyarbide said Cavallo tried "to benefit a company (Encotesa) which, although state-owned, was headed by a person who, as is widespread public knowledge, is closely linked to Cavallo" -- Encotesa chief Haroldo Grisanti, a close aide to the then minister.
The indictment is for "business interests incompatible with public office" and even says it cannot be ruled out that Cavallo made some personal profit.
Former Finance and Banking Secretary Roque Maccarone is also under indictment for allegedly advising Cavallo on the tender.

Interior Minister Corach, who like Justice Minister Elias Jassan is taking legal action against Cavallo for charges of manipulation of the legal system, said Tuesday he was "neither sad nor happy" about Cavallo's indictment.

Dismissing Cavallo's allegations that Judge Oyarbide's name was on a napkin on which Cavallo says Corach wrote the names of all the judges he controls, Corach told reporters in an ironic tone: "A napkin wouldn't be enough, you'd need a tablecloth."

Some backing for Cavallo came from the Auditor General Enrique Paixao, who told a news conference late Monday that in seven postal tenders for Argentine ministries, Yabran's firms were unfairly favored against state post office Encotesa.
